previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a right-handed male with composite Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for his sixth maintenance cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He tolerated the infusion well, with mild nausea managed by antiemetics. He developed acute kidney injury with elevated creatinine, consistent with acute tubular necrosis, which remained stable with hydration and urine alkalinization. A brain MRI showed no interval change, with the left frontal lesion unchanged and consistent with gliosis. CSF analysis showed no evidence of infection or malignant cells. Ocular radiation was planned for preventive treatment of ocular lymphoma. Constipation was managed with lactulose, docusate, and senna. He was discharged home in stable condition on aspirin, docusate, senna, and as-needed anti-nausea medications, with follow-up for radiation oncology and lab monitoring.

MR OF THE BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH IV GADOLINIUM: Overall, there

significant change in appearance of the brain compared to ___. 
There has been no change in a small focus of hyperintense

Brief Hospital Course:
CNS Lymphoma: Patient is presenting for his second maintainence 
cycle of high-dose methotrexate. He received IVF and bicarb per 
protocol to maintain a urine pH>8. His leucovorin was started 12 
hours (rather than the usual 24-hour) post-methotrexate given 
some increasing nausea and his priro elevated liver function 
tests. His methotrexate levels trended down appropriately. He 
was maintained on a methotrexate diet. He underwent an MRI of 
his brain prior to discharge to evaluate progression which 
appeared unchanged. He also received 1 dose of Rituximab prior 
to discharge for further treatment. However, during this 
infusion he developed rigors that resolved within minutes. This 
may have been a mild allergic reaction to the rituximab. He was 
unable to finish the infusion at a slower rate even though the 
rituximab was run at a slower rate. He then received 1,000 mg of 
solumedrol, and then a prednisone taper.

(1) Transaminitis: He had mild transaminitis during this 
admission, likely due to methotrexate, trending down by 
discharge.

___, M.D. in ___.  

(3) FEN: Fluids per methotrexate protocol, replete lytes prn, 
regular diet. No vitamin C, carbonated beverages, fruits, or 
citrous drinks  

(4) Prophylaxis: He will have a bowel regimen, HSC unless
